{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Step 1: Deduplicate on patient_id, keeping the row with highest sample_seq
# This ensures one row per patient, as per data dictionary
print('Shape before deduplication:', df.shape)

# Sort by patient_id and sample_seq (descending) to prepare for deduplication
df_sorted = df.sort_values(['patient_id', 'sample_seq'], ascending=[True, False])

# Drop duplicates on patient_id, keeping the first (highest sample_seq)
df_dedup = df_sorted.drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

print('Shape after deduplication:', df_dedup.shape)
print('Number of duplicate patient_ids before deduplication:', len(df) - len(df_dedup))

# Step 2: Filter for patients with severe disease (case-insensitive)
severe_dedup = df_dedup[df_dedup['severity'].str.lower() == 'severe']

print('Number of unique patients with severe disease after deduplication:', len(severe_dedup))

# Step 3: Filter out rows where biomarker_baseline is -999 (QC failure)
severe_clean = severe_dedup[severe_dedup['biomarker_baseline'] != -999]

print('Number of valid baseline values for severe patients after deduplication:', len(severe_clean))

# Step 4: Compute mean baseline biomarker value (ng/mL)
mean_baseline_severe = severe_clean['biomarker_baseline'].mean()
print('Mean baseline biomarker value (ng/mL) for severe patients (after deduplication):', mean_baseline_severe)"}
